answer: A marble counts only after the forge strikes it and the inlet hears that strike's decay. The decay carries the grip of the one key that held the marble, so a copied description has nothing for the inlet to measure. Keys that strike in the same instant blend into one decay, and a blended grip matches no single key. Splitting the marble breaks the decay in half, so each fragment fails the inlet. A ring saved after the marble has left the forge is ignored, because the inlet measures the stone while the forge is still closed around it.
